subject: regional-sanskrit
title: Sanskrit — Set 1
description: Basic vocabulary: everyday words in Sanskrit

questions.question: What does 'जलम्' (Jalam) mean in Sanskrit?
questions.explanation: 'जलम्' means water in Sanskrit. Water is one of the five elements (Panchabhutas).

questions.question: What does 'सूर्यः' (Suryah) mean?
questions.explanation: 'सूर्यः' means Sun. Many Indian names (Surya, Suraj) come from this Sanskrit word.

questions.question: How do you say 'one' in Sanskrit?
questions.explanation: 'एकम्' means one in Sanskrit. Numbers: एकम् (1), द्वे (2), त्रीणि (3), चत्वारि (4).

questions.question: What does 'पुस्तकम्' (Pustakam) mean?
questions.explanation: 'पुस्तकम्' means book. The modern Hindi word 'पुस्तक' comes from this Sanskrit word.

questions.question: What does 'मित्रम्' (Mitram) mean?
questions.explanation: 'मित्रम्' means friend in Sanskrit. 'Mitra' also means the Sun (a deity) in Vedic literature.

questions.question: What does 'वनम्' (Vanam) mean?
questions.explanation: 'वनम्' means forest or wood. Many Indian place names with 'van/ban' come from this root.

questions.question: What does 'चन्द्रः' (Chandrah) mean?
questions.explanation: 'चन्द्रः' means Moon. The name 'Chandra' and the word 'chandelier' share this root.

questions.question: Which letter does the Sanskrit alphabet (varnamala) begin with?
questions.explanation: The Sanskrit varnamala begins with the vowel 'अ' (a). Vowels (स्वर) come before consonants (व्यंजन).

questions.question: What does 'गृहम्' (Griham) mean?
questions.explanation: 'गृहम्' means house or home. The word 'griha' is used in many Indian languages.

questions.question: What does 'नमः' (Namah) mean?
questions.explanation: 'नमः' means salutation or bow. 'नमस्ते' (Namaste) = नमः + ते, meaning 'I bow to you'.
